rationale: Keep Granite Solar Portfolio as its own canonical portfolio record and do not merge it into a synthetic US Solar Fund aggregate. US Solar Fund's current portfolio page and audited 2025 reporting consistently treat Granite as a distinct eight-asset, 39 MWdc North Carolina acquisition portfolio, separately from Milford, Olympos, Heelstone and Euryalus. USF acquired 100% of the cash equity interests in the eight projects in January 2020, and its 2025 annual report continues to identify Granite as a separate current portfolio with project-level operating disclosures. Amber remains USF's investment manager. The May 2026 potential whole-portfolio sale was only a non-binding letter of intent subject to due diligence and definitive documentation, so it does not establish a signed pending exit or justify an ownership change. No company, seed, ownership, redirect, pending-transaction or publication mutation is authorized by this task.

identityResolution.portfolioBoundary: Eight operating North Carolina solar projects totaling 39 MWdc, acquired together by US Solar Fund in January 2020 and reported as the Granite portfolio.
identityResolution.sourceJudgmentCorrection: The prior MATCHED_ELSEWHERE note grouped Granite under a broad US Solar Fund U.S. Solar Portfolio. Current primary evidence supports keeping the separately named acquisition portfolio, while treating the broad fund-wide label as a manager aggregate rather than a duplicate canonical company.

acquisitionExitCheck.acquisitionSearch: US Solar Fund's current Granite page states that it acquired 100% of the cash equity interests in five projects on 2 January 2020 and the remaining three on 13 January 2020. The audited 2025 annual report separately identifies Granite as eight assets totaling 39 MWdc and records the January 2020 acquisition from Greenbacker Renewable Energy.
acquisitionExitCheck.exitSearch: US Solar Fund's May 2026 shareholder presentation disclosed a non-binding letter of intent for a possible sale of the entire 41-project portfolio, with a 90-day exclusivity period, due diligence and definitive documentation still required. No definitive sale agreement or closing was identified.
acquisitionExitCheck.currentOwnership: US Solar Fund continues to report the Granite portfolio as eight current operating assets within its 41-project portfolio. Amber Infrastructure Investment Advisor, LLC remains USF's investment manager.
